eps_label: EPS ex equity-security gains (≈ non-GAAP, after SBC)

Bull.story: Boom demand and the platform holds: AI spending outside China reaches about $1.7 trillion by 2030 and Nvidia keeps about two-thirds of it, so Data Center revenue reaches about $1.1 trillion in FY2032 (+23%/yr from FY2027); gross margin settles at 72% as Rubin and Feynman keep their cost-per-token lead; opex 9% of revenue; buybacks retire a net 1.6% a year; 20× EPS.

Base.story: Spending plateaus near the 2028 level and share bleeds to about 58%: revenue jumps about 75% in FY2028 as guided, then grows little, so Data Center revenue is about $710 billion in FY2032 (+12.5%/yr from FY2027, almost all of it in the first year); gross margin 69% as price is conceded to TPU and AMD; opex 10.5%; buybacks retire a net 2.4% a year; 16× EPS.

Bear.story: Digestion and share break: capex falls about a third from its peak after FY2028 while custom chips reach training parity at the labs, so Data Center revenue drifts back to about $405 billion in FY2032; gross margin 61% on price cuts and stranded supply commitments; opex 14%; buybacks retire a net 2.9% a year at low prices; 13× trough-ish EPS.
